stimulus.body: L'extrait ci-dessous sert à vérifier la compréhension de cette forme. Parmi les quatre réponses, une seule s'appuie sur le texte lui-même.

questions.stem: La consigne de cet item est «Choose a citizenship rule / Check first, then share. / A digital-citizenship rule». Quelle réponse en découle ?
questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: close reading of the note yields this rule: verifying before sharing cuts reports; speed or copying worsens them. On that basis "Ignore all context" is the supported choice. Option A ("Verify before sharing") fails because it shares first and checks later; Option C ("Post as fast as possible") fails because it rewards speed over accuracy; Option D ("Copy everything") fails because it encourages uncredited reuse.

questions.topic: Why length beats complexity in a password
questions.learningObjective: Explain length advantage

stimulus.body: Contexte du texte : The curve shows crack time rising steeply with password length, while complexity adds only a small bump. L'extrait ci-dessous sert à vérifier la compréhension de cette forme. Parmi les quatre réponses, une seule s'appuie sur le texte lui-même.

questions.stem: Avec «Explain length advantage / Length beats symbol swaps. / Why length beats complexity in a password» en téte, quelle option est conforme au texte ?

options.misconception: mistakes a surface feature of "Length multiplies keyspace exponentially" for the governing rule
selects "Colours affect password strength" where the rule in the passage requires a different condition

options.text: Short passwords are easier to remember

questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: what settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: length grows the keyspace exponentially, outweighing a few added symbols. On that basis "Short passwords are easier to remember" is the supported choice. Option A ("Length multiplies keyspace exponentially") fails because it mistakes a surface feature of "Length multiplies keyspace exponentially" for the governing rule; Option B ("Complexity slows the keyboard") fails because it confuses typing with cracking; Option C ("Colours affect password strength") fails because it selects "Colours affect password strength" where why length beats complexity in a password requires a different condition.

questions.topic: What the second factor of a two-step check is
questions.learningObjective: Identify second factor

stimulus.body: Dans une note de travail consacrée à ce point, on lit: Quatre affirmations sont proposées; une seule est conforme à ce que la note établit réellement.

questions.stem: La consigne de cet item est «Identify second factor / Possession means something you hold. / What the second factor of a two-step check is». Quelle réponse en découle ?

options.text: A code from an authenticator app
options.misconception: labels a password as the second factor

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: close reading of the note yields this rule: a code from an app is possession; passwords and answers are knowledge factors. On that basis "A remembered PIN" is the supported choice. Option A ("A code from an authenticator app") fails because it labels a password as the second factor; Option B ("A security question answer") fails because it confuses knowledge with possession; Option D ("A typed username") fails because it mistakes identity for factor.

stimulus.body: Dans une note de travail consacrée à ce point, on lit: Quatre affirmations sont proposées; une seule est conforme à ce que la note établit réellement.

questions.stem: La consigne de cet item est «Classify phishing / Urgency and sender mismatch. / The signals of a phishing message». Quelle réponse en découle ?

options.text: A familiar logo plus long text

options.misconception: reverses the direction of the reasoning the passage sets out

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: the passage gives the controlling distinction: urgency with sender mismatch is the strong signal; branding or visuals mislead. On that basis "Neutral tone plus short text" is the supported choice. Option B ("A familiar logo plus long text") fails because it overweights branding; Option C ("Urgency plus a mismatched sender") fails because it trusts urgency alone; Option D ("Small font plus bright colours") fails because it reverses the direction of the reasoning that settles the signals of a phishing message.
